clue.text: Leader of the Jets, flashy, is hard to be ignored in film

parts.note: Riff leads the Jets gang in West Side Story

indicators.note: these words tell us the letters given by 'is hard' drop out of the flashy word

parts.note: flashy, showily disreputable, is raffish
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A film critic describes the showy gang leader from West Side Story, whose toughness goes unnoticed on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be ignored' removes IS and H (hard) from RAFFISH, leaving RAFF. Riff is the leader of the Jets in West Side Story.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-Raff is a 1991 Ken Loach picture about building-site workers, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Film director's trailer about soldiers

indicators.note: the climbing plant goes round, about, the soldiers

parts.note: ivy is a trailing climbing plant, so a trailer
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A director's film preview turns out to feature troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' looks like a film preview but is a trailing plant. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: James Ivory directed Merchant Ivory pictures such as A Room with a View, so he is an instance of a director.

clue.text: Film star far steadier dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the two words are rearranged; apt for a famous hoofer

explanation.surface: A movie star is said to be much steadier on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges FAR STEADIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was a Hollywood dancer and leading man of the 1930s musicals, so an instance of a star.

clue.text: Actress rented farm beneath wood

indicators.note: in a down clue the farm sits below the wood

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
a croft is a small rented farm, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: An actress lives on a tenancy farm below the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: A croft is a smallholding in the Scottish Highlands, traditionally rented by its crofter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Peggy Ashcroft was a celebrated English stage and screen performer, an example of an actress.

clue.text: Arranged do for Tiptoes set film technician

indicators.note: arranged letters are put in a new order, so the four words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A set is prepared for a tiptoeing scene to be filmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges DO FOR TIPTOES SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A footsteps editor is the sound specialist who adds the walking noises to a soundtrack, a kind of film technician.

clue.text: Film with Gregory Peck in storm on motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue the storm word comes on, after, the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: A Gregory Peck film is caught in a tempest on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway, its 1 read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirage is a 1965 thriller in which Gregory Peck plays an amnesiac, a picture he starred in.

clue.text: Canadian actor shot in billiards controversy, ultimately

parts.note: a massé is a billiards shot with a steeply angled cue

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of controversy

explanation.surface: A Canadian actor's billiards stroke ends in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Massey was a Toronto-born Hollywood performer, so an example of a Canadian actor.

clue.text: Play game right

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: An instruction to play a game properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb but names a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: R.U.R. is Karel Čapek's 1920 drama that introduced the word robot, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Conservationist to shoot film

parts.note: a green is an environmental campaigner
to shoot a gun is to fire it

explanation.surface: An environmentalist sets out to shoot a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests filming but means fire a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Green Fire is a 1954 adventure picture with Grace Kelly and Stewart Granger, an example of a film.

clue.text: The subject of a musical, opening in Jerusalem, with high hopes

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters of hopes are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stage musical begins in Jerusalem full of optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like it qualifies hopes but signals a rearrangement of HOPES.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat is a Lloyd Webber show built around the biblical figure, so he is its subject.

clue.text: Shown in a film concerning partition

parts.note: on can mean about, concerning
a screen is a dividing partition

explanation.surface: Something displayed in a movie deals with a dividing wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appearing on-screen is seen in a movie or on television, i.e. displayed.

clue.text: Ms Breckinridge, perhaps a contrary Mary?

indicators.note: contrary suggests going against order, so the letters of Mary are rearranged; a nod to the nursery rhyme

parts.note: the four letters of Mary are the fodder; that they also run backwards across contrary Mary is a coincidence of the anagram

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Ms Breckinridge is the nursery rhyme's quite contrary Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' recalls 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' but rearranges MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Myra Breckinridge is the title character of Gore Vidal's novel and its 1970 film, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Italian film director and composer crossing the Spanish lake

indicators.note: the composer stretches across, around, the other letters

parts.note: Gioachino Rossini wrote The Barber of Seville
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An Italian director and a composer cross a lake in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberto Rossellini made Rome, Open City and other neorealist pictures, so he is an Italian director.

clue.text: Little Richard song and dance leaving American actress

parts.note: Lucille is a 1957 Little Richard rock and roll hit
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A song and dance by Little Richard drives away an American actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' is only a link here, in the sense of producing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucille Ball starred in the sitcom I Love Lucy, so she is an example of a US comedienne and screen performer.

clue.text: Sleeveless coat on prostitute, a Molière character

indicators.note: in an across clue the coat comes on, after, the prostitute

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute

indicators.note: sleeves hang at the sides, so the coat word loses its two outer letters

parts.note: a puffer is a padded quilted jacket

explanation.surface: A streetwalker wears a sleeveless jacket, like a figure from French comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeveless' removes the ends P and R from PUFFER, leaving UFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartuffe is the religious hypocrite who gives his name to Molière's 1664 comedy, a figure from that playwright's work.

clue.text: The making of cartoons may get one male in a state

parts.note: a nation is a state
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Producing cartoons could win a man some fame across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and M within A NATION, after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is the process of drawing and filming successive frames to create cartoons.

clue.text: Extract from film about border

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
a lip is a rim or border

explanation.surface: A cinema excerpt covers a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a short excerpt taken from a movie, as shown on chat shows.

clue.text: Awful ham, pants in horror film

explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges HAM PANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantasm is a 1979 cult horror picture about the sinister Tall Man, an instance of a horror film.

clue.text: Film produced by two US soldiers

indicators.note: two calls for the soldier abbreviation twice

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A movie made by a pair of American servicemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is the 1958 Lerner and Loewe musical picture that won nine Oscars, an example of a film.

clue.text: US producer of singular film that arouses terror?

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.walkthrough: Schiller suggests the German poet, but here it is a US producer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Schiller is an American film producer and director, so an example of a US producer.

clue.text: Bishop in Wesker play and film

parts.note: Roots is Arnold Wesker's 1959 play
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop appears in a play by Arnold Wesker and in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Robots is a 2005 computer-animated picture from Blue Sky Studios, an example of a film.

clue.text: Actor, TV foil of 13, in orange and gold combination

indicators.note: a combination mixes things together, so the colour words are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A television actor is dressed in orange and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination' rearranges ORANGE GOLD. Gale Gordon played the blustering bank manager opposite the star of 13-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gale Gordon was the comic stooge to the actress at 13 in The Lucy Show, so her TV foil.

clue.text: In verse, a stage play by Berkoff

indicators.note: In says the answer is held within the words verse a stage

explanation.surface: A verse drama by Steven Berkoff is put on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'versE A STage'.
explanation.definitionFit: East is Steven Berkoff's 1975 verse drama of London's East End, so it is one of his plays.

clue.text: A young man who is in love with Lolita in the film

definitions.text: A young man who is in love
definitions.meaning: a lovestruck youth, a suitor in pastoral poetry
Dominique ... played the title role in Adrian Lyne's 1997 film of Lolita

explanation.surface: A lovesick youth falls for Lolita in the movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a poetic word for a youthful lover, and Dominique Swain was Lolita on screen.

clue.text: Being crazy, no end, about old Hitchcock film

parts.note: being, existence, is life

the crazy word loses its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts the last letter from BATS; 'about' puts what is left around O, from 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeboat is Hitchcock's 1944 wartime drama set entirely in a drifting rescue boat, one of his pictures.

clue.text: Actor, Trevor, in The Verdict

indicators.note: in says the answer is held within the words The Verdict

explanation.surface: Trevor the actor appears in a courtroom film.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'thE VErdict'.

clue.text: Film a king on a vessel

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquid

explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat but is a tank.

clue.text: Financial backers of TV hospital drama series

definitions.meaning: theatrical investors who fund a production
A 1970s BBC series about student nurses

clue.text: Actress phoned about phoney limp
